title: Colorado Springs Insulation Rebates 2026: 40% Up to $1,250 from Springs Utilities
desc: Colorado Springs Utilities pays 40% of cost up to $1,250 each for attic, wall and crawl space insulation in 2026. R-values, permit rules, contractor rules and the January 31 deadline.
badge: 40% back, up to $1,250 for each type of insulation
lead: Colorado Springs Utilities pays one of the larger insulation rebates in Colorado: 40% of the job, up to $1,250 each for the attic, the walls and the crawl space. It also has stricter rules than most, including R-values you must hit and a ban on do-it-yourself work.
cards_heading: What insulation rebates pay in Colorado Springs
cards_intro: We read the Colorado Springs Utilities 2026 rebate form and rebate rules on October 5, 2026. Xcel's rebates do not apply here, because Colorado Springs Utilities is your utility, and the utility's program replaces them.

cards.title: Attic insulation
cards.note: Needs R-49, and the job must include sealing the bypasses, which are hidden air paths from your living space into the attic.

cards.title: Wall insulation
cards.note: Needs R-13 in the wall cavity, or continuous exterior insulation of R-5 or more. Living space only, not garages.

cards.title: Crawl space insulation
cards.note: Needs R-15 continuous insulation and a Class I vapor barrier, plus air sealing of the space. The form lists the same $1,250 cap.

cards.title: State income-based rebates (HEAR)
cards.note: Up to $1,600 for insulation and air sealing while open. El Paso County was in the Front Range region, now closed.

after_cards:
Working it out

An attic job that costs $2,800 earns 40%, or $1,120, which is under the $1,250 cap. A $4,000 attic job would earn $1,600 at 40%, but the cap holds it at $1,250. Do the attic, the walls and the crawl space and each can earn up to $1,250 on its own, so a whole-house job could reach $3,750 in rebates. The rules also say the insulation total must meet Department of Energy recommendations, which includes the attic and the exterior walls together, so ask your contractor how that is judged for your home.
sections: What Colorado Springs homes look like

The American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) counts 211,353 homes in Colorado Springs. About 61% of households own and 39% rent. Around 60% are detached houses, and only 6% are in buildings of two to four units. About 39% were built before 1980 and only 5% before 1940, while 30% were built in 2000 or later.

The utility's rule covers residential buildings of four or fewer units and three stories or under, with no central mechanical system serving several units. A detached house or a small duplex fits easily. A larger apartment building does not, so owners of those buildings should ask about the business rebate program.
The rules that trip people up

Colorado Springs Utilities has requirements that other utilities do not. Work must be done by a Colorado contractor, and do-it-yourself work does not qualify. The attic job must include air sealing at the bypasses. The insulation has to meet the stated R-value, and the rebate applies to living quarters only, not garages. You must be a Colorado Springs Utilities electric and/or gas customer. The rebate is paid as a credit on your account, which can take up to eight weeks.

Installation must happen between January 1 and December 31, 2026, and the application must be postmarked by January 31, 2027. Attach an itemized receipt with the contractor's information on company letterhead. Rebates are first come, first served and depend on available funds. If you are denied, the rules give you 60 days to ask about it.

About 70% of Colorado Springs households heat with utility gas and 27% with electricity. The utility sells both, so the insulation rebate works for either fuel. If you heat with gas, the saving comes from using less gas. If you heat with electricity, the saving is larger per dollar, since electric heat costs more per unit of heat. If you plan to add a heat pump, see our Colorado Springs heat pump page, since insulation first can let you buy a smaller one.

Our climate file, built from ten Januaries (2015 to 2024), shows an average January low of about 17°F and a coldest day near minus 25°F. The attic rule asks for R-49, which is high, and Colorado Springs Utilities says total insulation must meet Department of Energy recommendations, so a thin top-up may not be enough to qualify.
installers_intro: Ranked by Google reviews (minimum five). We don't take referral fees or paid placements. Ask each one whether they have done Colorado Springs Utilities rebate jobs and whether the contractor letterhead invoice and R-values will be on the paperwork.
claim_heading: How to claim Colorado Springs insulation rebates
claim_steps: Confirm that Colorado Springs Utilities sends your electric and/or gas bill.
Ask for quotes that state the R-value and include air sealing at the attic bypasses.
Use a Colorado contractor, since do-it-yourself work does not qualify.
Keep an itemized receipt on contractor letterhead.
Apply by email, mail or My Account so it is postmarked by January 31, 2027.
